explanation: Singapore's business culture places a high value on punctuality, and arriving late to a meeting is seen as a lack of respect for the other person's time. If you're unavoidably delayed, calling or messaging ahead is expected and softens the impact considerably.
local_tip: Aim to arrive 5-10 minutes early, and if you're running late, notify your host as soon as you know rather than waiting until the meeting time has passed.

also_check.note: Punctuality norms are even stricter; arriving even a few minutes late is seen as disrespectful and often requires a sincere apology.
Social gatherings allow more flexibility, but arriving late to a first business meeting is still risky.
Social events often start later than scheduled, but business meetings generally still expect punctuality.

sources.title: Laws and Etiquette to Keep in Mind on a Business Trip to Singapore
